evidence_items.explanation: Accuracy declined as digit ranges increased, even after additional training on longer examples. This supports a continuing reliability weakness, although mixed arithmetic operations and exposure to longer examples prevent treating it as a clean test of wholly unseen lengths.

Models trained on five-digit addition achieved 99.9% accuracy on ten-digit inputs and 98.3% on fifteen-digit inputs, demonstrating substantial transfer beyond training lengths. Accuracy fell to 21.3% at twenty digits, so the success qualifies an absolute inability claim while remaining compatible with a persistent weakness.
